# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

## Goal

Execute the 24-hour experiment: apply the STE100 instruction to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, let it run for 24h, measure metrics, produce comparison report, and revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add the sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (verified via grep).
2. Record exact wall-clock T0 and commit hash.
3. Run analysis at T0+24h for both [T0-24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) windows.
4. Produce comparison report at `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` with:
   - Metrics table (session count, duration, tokens, cost for both windows)
   - Delta percentages and direction for each metric
   - Notable outliers (output-token-limit errors, extreme sessions)
   - Project and model breakdown
   - One-line interpretation per metric
5. Revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (verified via grep).
6. Record revert commit hash.

## Steps

1. Start parent implementation
2. Implement child tasks first (analysis script + tests)
3. Add STE100 sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev, record T0
4. Wait 24 hours (or set reminder/automation)
5. Run analysis for baseline window [T0-24h, T0)
6. Run analysis for experiment window [T0, T0+24h)
7. Generate comparison report
8. Revert AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev
9. Record results on work item
10. Clean up worktree

## Related

Dependent on: SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (Build analysis script), SA-0MU9VT5HI001LHKY (Add tests).

Create the whisper worker protocol — persistent Python worker and TypeScript client.

**Files:**
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — TypeScript client
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — Python worker process

**whisper-client.ts responsibilities:**
- Spawn whisper_worker.py with configurable model/device/compute args
- Implement line-delimited JSON protocol (worker reads stdin, writes JSONL to stdout)
- Protocol messages: START (model init), FEED (PCM chunk), FINALISE (get transcript), STOP
- Handle partial transcripts: emit events as they arrive
- Handle errors: forward worker stderr/exit code as error events
- Lifecycle: init on recording start, feed PCM frames during recording, finalise on stop, clean exit

**whisper_worker.py responsibilities:**
- Import faster-whisper on startup
- Load model once (device + compute_type from config, with CPU int8 fallback)
- Run a loop: read JSON commands from stdin, write JSON responses to stdout
- FEED accumulates audio, transcribes at configurable cadence
- FINALISE returns the complete transcript
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM

**Unit tests (TDD — mock the Python worker process):**
- START message spawns worker and waits for READY response
- FEED messages buffer data and trigger partial transcript callbacks
- FINALISE collects all buffered data and returns final transcript
- STOP sends SHUTDOWN, waits for ACK, verifies clean exit
- Worker stderr/exit code produces error events, never crashes the client
data.title: Whisper worker protocol: persistent Python worker and TypeScript client

# Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done

**Recurring defect — producer has raised this repeatedly.** Policy restated by the producer (2026-10-02): *if a parent is marked `completed` and it has been audited, then all its children are considered complete.* The concrete fix requested: **when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `status=completed, stage=done`.**

## Problem statement

When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent work item, its descendants are left in whatever terminal or non-terminal state they previously held. This lets a parent reach `status=completed, stage=in_review` with a passing audit while its children remain `open`/`blocked`/`in_progress` (or already `done`), so downstream steps can neither treat the subtree as consistent nor close the parent without a manual `wl close --force` sweep.

## Users and user stories

- **Primary user — release producer.** As a producer, when I audit a parent work item and the audit passes, I want every descendant to be marked `completed`/`done` automatically so that I never have to force-close the parent and sweep unfinished children as a side effect.
- **Secondary user — the ship pipeline (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`).** As the post-release close step, I want an audit-approved parent's descendants to already be terminal so the collateral-descendant guard does not falsely refuse to close released items.
- **Secondary user — audit operators/agents.** As an audit operator, I want the cascade to be idempotent and authorised only by a passing parent audit, so reruns and failed audits never resurrect or mutate work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Cascade on passing parent audit.** When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent item (`readyToClose === true`, i.e. `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` on the success path), every descendant is set to `status=completed, stage=done`, and each cascaded child receives an explanatory comment naming the authorising parent and the audit timestamp.
- [ ] **AC2 — Idempotent and `deleted`-safe.** Re-running the cascade on an already-terminal tree produces no further mutations or duplicate comments; `deleted` descendants are skipped; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
- [ ] **AC3 — No cascade without a passing audit.** A parent audit that fails (`Ready to close: No`), is fallback-tainted, or has not been run performs **no** cascade and leaves descendants untouched. Cascading is authorised by a passing audit verdict only — never by status/stage alone.
- [ ] **AC4 — Ship close step closes the parent without a refusal.** `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` closes a parent whose descendants are all terminal (`done`/`deleted`) without a refusal, covered by unit tests that inject `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn` (overlaps SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP tasks).
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression tests cover the behaviour.** Passing-parent → children done (with comments); failing-parent → children untouched; parent with a mix of `deleted`/`done`/`open` children → only the appropriate action; cascade rerun → no further mutation (testing/validation criterion).
- [ ] **AC6 — Existing audit and ship suites pass.** The existing audit runner and ship suites pass and `npm run build` passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` as applicable).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The cascade must live where the verdict is known — the parent audit success path in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — not only as a special case inside the ship close step.
- Any `wl` mutations must respect the `StatusLifecycle` claim invariant (an item must be `in_progress` before mutation) and route `--worklog-dir` through the shared resolution helpers so the cascade targets the item's own worklog store regardless of cwd.
- The cascade must not weaken the existing scope guard (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H): a parent whose audit has **not** passed must still refuse to close over non-terminal descendants.
- Must remain safe under dry-run (`--do-not-persist`): a dry-run passing verdict must not mutate descendants.

## Existing state

- **Verdict knowledge.** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` computes the parent verdict at `audit_verdict = _parse_ready_to_close(report)` (~line 11363) and, in the terminal transition block, takes the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch (~line 11773) to run `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (or `--stage done` when already done). This is the natural single point to trigger the cascade.
- **Child-state checks today.** `_check_children_stages` / related helpers already classify children in `in_review`/`done` as exempt but do **not** mutate them; `inherited_pass` records a verdict reuse but never sets `completed`/`done`.
- **Ship close step.** `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (~line 370) computes `candidateIds` from `getCandidateItems()` (= `stage=in_review` only) and refuses a `--force` close when `collateral = descendants.filter(id => !candidateIds.has(id))` is non-empty (~line 534). Descendants already `stage=done` therefore always appear as collateral — tracked narrowly as SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP.
- **Evidence (TCE v0.1.19 release, 2026-10-02).** Five parents sat at `completed/in_review` after the release, all audit-approved; the close step refused all five (25 open/blocked children on two of them), and all five had to be closed with `wl close --force`, sweeping 50 descendants to `done`.

## Desired change

1. Add a cascade helper (e.g. `_cascade_descendants_terminal`) in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` that, given a parent id and audit timestamp, walks descendants (`wl show <id> --children` recursively or the existing tree helpers), skips `deleted` and already `completed`/`done` items, and for each remaining descendant issues `wl update <child> --status completed --stage done`, followed by `wl comment add <child>` with a reason naming the parent and audit timestamp.
2. Invoke the helper from the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success branch only (and not on the failure/fallback restore branches), after the parent's own verified transition succeeds; suppress it under dry-run.
3. Make the helper idempotent (no mutation/comment when a child is already terminal) and non-fatal (a cascade failure for one child is logged and does not abort the audit, matching the ship step's non-blocking semantics).
4. Keep `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`'s collateral logic unchanged apart from SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP's `done`/`deleted` exclusion (defence-in-depth).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Add the cascade helper and call it on the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success path; reuse existing descendant/`_run_wl` helpers.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — Ensure `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` excludes terminal (`done`/`deleted`) descendants from `collateral` (SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP); add/verify injected-fn unit coverage for AC4.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — New cascade regression tests (passing parent, failing parent, mixed child states, idempotent rerun, dry-run).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — Extend lifecycle-transition tests to assert cascade/no-cascade per verdict.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — Unit tests for the terminal-descendant non-refusal (AC4).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` — Document cascade-on-audit behaviour (AC7).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP** (open) — "Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`": the narrower ship-side workaround. This item is the root-cause counterpart; they should be implemented together (or this item's AC1–AC3 makes the ship-side workaround unnecessary, keeping SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP as defence-in-depth).
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (in-progress) — "Audit runner: pre-review child with `inherited_pass` bypasses children-stage block and summary claims all children in `in_review`/`done`": the likely mechanism by which parents reach `in_review` with open children; fixing it prevents the "unfinished children under a done parent" failure mode.
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** (completed) — "wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK": the original decision; cascade-on-audit is the missing enforcement.
- **SA-0MQIQQ164007HEAA** (completed) — "Parent audit should pass when all children's ACs are met".
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** (completed) — "Audit: parent-first child pass-through".
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** (completed) — the scope guard that must not regress.
- **SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE** (completed) — "Content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits" (automated find-related match).
- **SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X** (completed) — "Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable" (automated find-related match).
- **Provenance:** filed from the Tableau-Card-Engine v0.1.19 release retro (2026-10-02).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — scope creep into the ship step.** The root fix is audit-side; touching `run-release.js` beyond the terminal-descendant exclusion risks duplicating SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP. Mitigation: keep the ship change minimal and additive.
- **Risk — partial cascade on `wl` failure.** A mid-cascade `wl` failure could leave a subtree half-terminal. Mitigation: per-child try/except, loud logging, idempotent rerun, non-fatal semantics; the next audit success completes the cascade.
- **Risk — comment noise / non-idempotence.** Re-auditing a passing parent must not duplicate comments. Mitigation: skip already-terminal children before commenting; test the rerun path (AC2/AC5).
- **Risk — regression to the audit scope guard.** Cascading on a *failed* verdict would bypass SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H. Mitigation: cascade only on the `audit_verdict == "yes"` branch; explicit failing-parent test (AC3/AC5).
- **Assumption.** "Descendants" means the full recursive subtree of the audited parent (children, grandchildren, …), consistent with `wl close --force`'s recursive sweep.
- **Assumption.** A passing parent audit is the sole authorisation signal; `status`/`stage` alone never authorises a cascade.
- **Assumption.** `deleted` descendants are historical and must never be re-marked or commented on.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Are any clarifications required beyond the seed context? — **Answer (producer, via the filed work item SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP and the TCE v0.1.19 release retro, 2026-10-02):** No. The seed context specifies the policy, the concrete requested fix ("when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `completed`/`done`"), the desired behaviour (5 points), the acceptance criteria, and the related work. The interview was therefore skipped per the intake "seed context suffices" rule.
- **Q:** Where should the cascade live? — **Answer (producer, seed context, Desired behaviour §2):** In `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` on the parent audit success path — a single source of truth where the verdict is known — not only as a special case in the ship close step. Evidence: repository inspection confirms the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` branch (~`audit_runner.py:11773`) is the success transition point.
- **Q:** How should `deleted` and already-terminal descendants be treated? — **Answer (producer, seed context, Desired behaviour §3):** `deleted` children are left untouched; reruns are no-ops; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
data.title: Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done
